name: Envista Holdings Corp
business: Envista sells dental implants, orthodontics including Spark aligners, imaging systems and consumables to dentists, specialists, clinics and hospitals worldwide.

events.what: CEO Paul Keel also appointed Chairman; base salary raised to $1.3M and one-time $10M retention award ($5M RSUs, $5M TSR PSUs, four-year vesting); CFO Eric Hammes $1.5M PSU award
events.from: Envista President and CEO since 2024-05-01 (ex CEO Smiths Group, 3M)
events.source: 8-K 0001757073-26-000074 (period of report 2026-08-17; compensation amendment effective 2026-08-24; Chairman effective date not stated in extract)

events.what: Investor Day: medium-term outlook raised (core growth 2-5%, adjusted EBITDA growth 5-8%, EPS growth 7-11%)
New Chief Accounting Officer (internal Global Controller)
events.from: Envista VP Global Controller; ex CBRE

events.what: Small bolt-on acquisition, Versah (osseodensification); no Item 2.01 or 1.01 8-K

next_event.source: The promised Investor Day already took place on 2026-09-17 (document_id 222566) and gave growth ranges, not a margin level or year. No further framework event found; Q3 2026 results date not confirmed.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Since the March 2025 Capital Markets Day management guides EBITDA growth, not margin. The medium-term outlook (raised 2026-09-17) is 2-5% core growth and 5-8% adjusted EBITDA growth, which the CEO translated into about 50 bps of margin expansion a year with no end year. The old 22.5%-by-2026 target (2022 Investor Day, prior CEO) was abandoned. One-year guide: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA growth 11-14%.

statements.quote: If you grow the top line at 2%-5%, take the middle of that, you grow EBITDA 5%-8%, take the midpoint of that, you get about 50 basis points of margin expanse in a year. Pick whatever you want to call medium-term, you can just run that math out.
statements.speaker: Paul Keel

statements.quote: We're shifting our entire EBITDA growth range up a point, from 4%-7%-5%-8%. Expanding gross margins together with the productivity initiatives that I just outlined support our ability to grow profits even faster than sales.
statements.speaker: Paul Keel

statements.quote: Our new guidance for the full year 2026 is 3.5% to 4.5% core growth, 11% to 14% adjusted EBITDA growth, Adjusted EPS of $1.50 to $1.55, and free cash flow conversion of approximately 100%.
statements.speaker: Eric Hammes
statements.doc_title: Envista Holdings Corp Q2 2026 Earnings Call

street.gap_assumption: No target year, so FY2028 is used as a two-year test. FY2026 consensus margin 14.66% plus the CEO's about 50 bps a year for two years = 15.66% vs FY2028 consensus 15.50% (+17 bps); using the new outlook midpoints (EBITDA +6.5%, revenue +3.5% a year) the gap is +3 bps. Consensus already models +42 bps in FY2027. December fiscal year; Baba labels equal company years.

evidence_of_progress.note: Q1 2026 adj EBITDA margin 14.0% vs 12.8% (+121 bps, consensus actuals); Q2 2026 14.7% vs 12.4% (+230 bps, 8-K 0001757073-26-000063). FY2025 margin 13.7%, +190 bps. Delivery is real, but the street is already extrapolating it.

disqualifier_reason: Margin framing already reflected in consensus: the CEO's about 50 bps a year sits 3 to 17 bps above FY2028 consensus (15.5%), well under the 25 bps threshold, and FY2027 consensus already embeds +42 bps. Catalyst leg is also weak: the external CEO (2024-05-01) and CFO (2024-08-08) are both outside the 18-month window; the in-window events are the CEO adding the Chairman role with a $10M retention grant, one director and three small bolt-ons.
verdict: A turnaround already in the numbers: margins up about 300 bps under a 2024 CEO, framing is growth-rate only, and consensus models it.
open_questions: Does consensus move after the 2026-09-17 outlook raise, or did the street already sit at the new 5-8% EBITDA growth range?
How much do China VBP (ortho and implants, second half 2026) and the Q4 billing-day drag weigh on the FY2027 starting margin?
With the medium-term range framed only as growth, will management ever give a margin level for Spark or the whole company?
